concepts.label: Internal Component account (Couchbase Server)
concepts.reused_or_minted: minted - a genuinely distinct local-domain member type this page names: Couchbase Server's own internal processes (indexing, searching, replicating) run AS local-domain accounts with full administrative privileges, not as an external/service-account concept the registry has any equivalent for.

concepts.label: saslauthd (legacy LDAP/PAM support)

concepts.label: PAM (Pluggable Authentication Modules)
concepts.reused_or_minted: minted - a third external-auth mechanism this page documents, layered on top of saslauthd for Linux system-account authentication; distinct enough from LDAP/SAML to need its own id rather than folding into idp:saslauthd, since PAM authenticates against /etc/shadow rather than a directory server

relations.subject: idp:ldap-group
relations.reused_or_minted_predicate: reused - groupMembersInheritRole, stretched: the mapping is LDAP-group-maps-to-Couchbase-group rather than direct membership inheritance, but the net effect (a user acquires a Couchbase group's roles via an external grouping) is the same shape.
relations.evidence: If an LDAP group has previously been _mapped_ to a Couchbase-Server group, the user inherits the roles assigned to the Couchbase-Server group.

relations.subject: idp:ldap-group
relations.reused_or_minted_predicate: reused - doesNotSatisfy, stretched: this is a positive capability statement framed with a negative-requirement predicate (LDAP groups let UNREGISTERED users be authorized) - kept because it captures the same 'this route bypasses the usual requirement' shape doesNotSatisfy was minted for.
relations.evidence: Note that LDAP Groups thus allow users _not_ registered on Couchbase Server — even as _external_ — to be authorized.

relations.subject: idp:ldap
relations.reused_or_minted_predicate: reused - hasExecutionConstraint, stretched from topology/placement to authentication-order sequencing, capturing the stated lookup order.
relations.evidence: When a user attempts to authenticate, Couchbase Server always looks up their credentials in the same order: which is _Local_ first, and _External_ second.

relations.subject: idp:saml-attribute-mapping

notable_absence.finding: This page is entirely about authentication and identity-to-role MAPPING (LDAP groups, SAML attributes) - it comes right up to the edge of RBAC's role/privilege catalogue (it names 'the roles assigned to the Couchbase-Server user-group' repeatedly) but never names one specific role or privilege by its catalogue name. It is the third page in a row in this batch to talk fluently about roles in the abstract without grounding a single one - reinforcing the finding on authentication-overview.json.

cross_component_finding: revocationRevokesChannelAccess is reused here for a Server-side session-termination fact with none of its originating vocabulary (channels) present at all - a genuine stress case for whether the predicate name should be generalized (something like revocationCascades) now that a second, unrelated product needs its shape. Separately: idp:native-ldap and idp:saslauthd's mutual-exclusivity ('The two cannot be used simultaneously') is a hard cluster-wide configuration constraint that has no precedent predicate in the registry beyond doesNotSupport, which was not built for mutual exclusivity between two configuration MODES of the same feature (as against a statement not supporting a construct) - flagged as an approximate fit.
cross_product_finding: idp:saml-attribute-mapping is deliberately NOT merged with the promoted sso:group-mapping (Capella SSO). Both map federated-identity attributes to access grants, but the destination differs structurally: sso:group-mapping resolves to Capella teams/roles at the organization/project management-plane level, while this page's SAML attribute mapping resolves directly to Server's own local RBAC roles and user-groups - the same federation idea implemented on top of two disjoint role catalogues (capella-role:* vs rbac-model:role/roles.md's catalogue). No page states the two mechanisms are related, so the naming-collision rule keeps them apart; this is now the second SSO-adjacent concept pair (after auth:sso/auth:mfa) this batch has had to adjudicate, and unlike that pair this one is NOT reused - the destination-catalogue difference is judged too structural to share an id, whereas auth:sso/auth:mfa describe the login mechanism itself, upstream of any catalogue.
